STYLE — the common document style

Copy the head of this file into any document — the semantic rule in its comment travels with it. The style is inlined, so every document using it is a single file that renders anywhere, with no stylesheet, no script, no fonts and no network. Below is a specimen of every element the style covers, so the effect is visible without reading the CSS.

A second-level heading

Body text. Black on white, one serif column, forty-six ems wide. Inline code sits in the monospace face at slightly under the body size, so a path or an identifier does not tower over the sentence around it. A date is written 2026-09-10.

A third-level heading

For a division inside a section: the size of the body text, set in italic.

A blockquote, for a statement set apart from the argument around it.

An ordinary list, and beneath it the tighter ladder variant, for lists read as a sequence of rungs rather than as prose:

  • an ordinary list item
  • another
  1. a ladder item, spaced tighter
  2. another
  3. a third

Tables, for data with two axes

A table claims that its rows are comparable down each column. Where that is not true of the content, what is wanted is a definition list.

a header cellitalic, not bold
a body cellruled in black, top-aligned, so a long cell beside a short one still reads
code in a cellthe monospace face carries into cells unchanged

Definition lists, for a term and its description

a term
its description, indented, with the term set in italic to match a table's header cell
another term
one axis, not two — nothing here is comparable to anything else down a column

Preformatted blocks

Code and commands are a pre wrapping a code element; a bare pre is for preformatted text that is not code.

a preformatted block of code: ruled, monospace, and scrolling
sideways rather than wrapping, so a long command line
stays one line and stays copyable

Figures, for an actual image

A figure holds an image and its caption, and the image is either raster or vector. Both are inside the file, so the document stays one file, and both are ruled in black like a table and never wider than the column. The alt text, or an svg's title, says what the image shows. The caption says what the image is and where it came from; for a rendering that means the source and the renderer, since a rendering is derived and not the thing itself. A diagram drawn in text is a preformatted block, not a figure.

A raster image, made of pixels, is an img whose source is a data URI. Its caption names its resolution, because pixels are all it has:

A vector image, made of shapes, is an svg written inline, with a viewBox and its intended width and height. It stays sharp at any size and can be read in the source. Its caption has no resolution to name:

A paragraph in the meta class: smaller, for the line under a title that says what a document is, and for a closing note on provenance.
